privacy.title: Privacy & security
privacy.description: What is stored, where, and what leaves your computer.
privacy.modeDescription: Blurs amounts and numbers on screen, for example while screen sharing or in a cafe. You can also turn it on from the button at the bottom of the menu.
privacy.storedDescription: Everything stays on this computer. No account, no cloud.
privacy.storedTransactions: Transactions, categories, budgets and goals - in the database file (spent.db).
privacy.storedCredentials: Bank logins, the AI provider API key and the bot token - encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
privacy.storedKey: The encryption key - in .encryption-key in the same folder, readable only by your user.
privacy.storedSettings: Display preferences such as privacy mode and the collapsed menu - in the browser only.
privacy.leavesDescription: Only what you turned on, and only to these places.
privacy.leavesBanks: Banks and card companies - your login goes only to the bank's own site, during a sync.
privacy.leavesAi: A cloud AI provider, if you chose one - the transaction description and amount only, without account, card or ID numbers. With local Ollama nothing leaves.
privacy.leavesTelegram: Telegram, if you linked a bot - only the summaries you ask for, only to the linked chat.
privacy.leavesUpdate: Update check against GitHub - none of your data, only whether a new version exists.
privacy.protectBody: Turn on disk encryption (BitLocker on Windows, FileVault on Mac). Anyone who can read the data folder can read your transactions. A backup of the folder includes the encryption key - keep it somewhere encrypted.
privacy.deleteDescription: Delete all transactions and category memory in one step. Bank connections are removed separately on the Bank accounts page.
privacy.lockDescription: Asks for a passphrase to open Penny and locks after idle time. The encryption key is stored wrapped with the passphrase, so a copy of the data folder does not expose bank logins. After a restart, unlock once so scheduled sync and the bot can work. Forgot it? The only way back is to delete everything.
privacy.lockHint: At least 8 characters, or a PIN of 6 or more digits.
privacy.lockError_wait: Too many tries. Try again shortly.
privacy.lockError_weak: Too short: at least 8 characters, or a 6-digit PIN.
privacy.wipeDescription: Deletes everything: transactions, bank connections and logins, settings, AI keys, the bot, the encryption key and logs. Penny returns to a fresh install. This cannot be undone.

legacy.title: If something happens to me
legacy.description: A calm, orderly document for your partner and family: where the money is, what gets paid and what to do. It builds itself from your data, and you can add your own words.
legacy.privacyNotice: This document is saved only on this computer. It contains no passwords. Keep a copy somewhere safe and tell someone you trust about it.
legacy.notesDescription: Saved automatically when you move to the next field. Write simply, like a note to someone close. No passwords or codes.
legacy.saveError: We couldn't save right now. Please try again in a moment.
legacy.docIntro: If you are holding this, it is probably a hard time. There is no need to do everything now. What matters is gathered here, and you can go one step at a time. Amounts are approximate, as of the update date.
legacy.stepsIntro: There is no required order, and nobody has to do it alone. Ask a relative, the accountant or the lawyer for help.
legacy.defaultSteps:
Breathe. No big money decisions are needed in the first weeks.
Get several copies of the death certificate.
Contact the banks and card companies with the death certificate, and later with the inheritance or probate order.
Check Har HaKesef (Ministry of Finance) for pension, provident and study funds.
Check Har HaBituach for insurance policies, and contact the insurers.
Notify Bituach Leumi and ask about survivors' benefits.
Go over recurring charges and cancel subscriptions that are no longer needed.
Ask the accountant or lawyer about an inheritance or probate order.

mortgageCalc.tracksHint: Banks split a mortgage into tracks. Prime moves with the Bank of Israel rate; fixed stays the same; fixed-linked has a lower rate, but the balance grows with the CPI.

mortgageCalc.warnShares: The track shares add up to {total}%. They should add up to 100%.
mortgageCalc.warnFixed: Bank of Israel rules require at least {min}% of the mortgage at a fixed rate.
mortgageCalc.warnLtv: The loan is {ltv}% of the property value. For a first home banks lend up to {max}%.
mortgageCalc.warnPtiOver: The payment is {pti}% of your income. Banks won’t approve more than 50%.
mortgageCalc.warnPtiHigh: The payment is {pti}% of your income. Above 40% leaves little room for surprises.
mortgageCalc.tip: Try a prime change of +2 points: if the higher payment still fits comfortably, the mix is safe. Every extra shekel you pay early on the most expensive track saves the most.
mortgageCalc.disclaimer: Rates are examples; take offers from at least three banks or a mortgage advisor.
